note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: RL query rewriting adapts to retrievers; retriever-specific dialects, guidance and scale shape what is learned

nodes.name: Retrievers need different query styles
nodes.description: Different retrievers require different optimal query formulation strategies, but most agentic RAG work assumes a uniform single search engine.

nodes.name: Retrievers' training and nature differ
nodes.description: Contriever is trained on Wikipedia span pairs and prefers document-style queries, BM25 is sparse and prefers keyword queries, and Qwen3-Embedding performs better with question-like queries.

nodes.name: GRPO rewriter with nDCG@10 reward
nodes.description: The query rewriter policy is trained with GRPO using nDCG@10 of the retrieved documents against the ground-truth passage as reward, chosen over recall to reward ranking the correct document highly.

nodes.name: RL improves in-distribution retrieval
nodes.description: On RAGBench, RL-trained rewriters improve every tested retriever, e.g., Contriever average nDCG@10 from 45.5 to 56.3 (direct), BM25 from 45.0 to 56.9 (explore), Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B from 61.5 to 64.1.

nodes.name: Zero-shot BEIR transfer
nodes.description: Zero-shot on BEIR, the learned rewriter raises Contriever's average from 28.84 to 34.98, whereas Gemini-2.5-Flash rewrites reduce performance even with a Contriever-specific prompt.

nodes.name: Domain transfer to finance
nodes.description: On FinAgentBench, the rewriter improves Contriever (6.43 to 7.39), BM25 (8.17 to 9.02), all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (6.69 to 7.17) and Qwen3-Embedding (9.10 to 10.81).

nodes.name: RE-MMD separates semantic and structural drift
nodes.description: RE-MMD measures the distance between distributions of successful queries across retrievers, split into semantic (intent) drift and structural (formulation) drift.

nodes.name: Drift is structural, not semantic
nodes.description: Semantic RE-MMD is typically below 2.0 while structural RE-MMD is often above 20.0, largest between sparse (BM25) and dense (Contriever) retrievers, so transfer failures are stylistic rather than about information need.

nodes.name: Strategies don't transfer across retrievers
nodes.description: Query formulation policies optimized for one retriever generally do not transfer reliably to others.

nodes.name: Prompt guidance levels
nodes.description: Three prompt levels were compared: general (five candidate strategies, retriever unknown), exploratory (retriever and its training described), and specific (human-prescribed strategy, e.g., hypothetical documents for Contriever, keywords for BM25).

nodes.name: Contriever: specific prompt wins
nodes.description: For Contriever, the exploratory prompt starts strongest but collapses early (around step 200) onto a keyword strategy, while the specific prompt enforcing hypothetical documents reaches the best final performance; the general prompt improves slowly.

nodes.name: BM25: exploratory beats specific
nodes.description: For BM25, exploratory prompts outperform specific ones and both far exceed general prompts; the rewriter infers keyword queries early, plausibly because BM25 is well documented in LLM pretraining data.

nodes.name: Human guidance helps when priors are weak
nodes.description: Explicit human expert guidance helps RL when the model lacks knowledge of a retriever's optimal strategy, whereas exploratory prompts suffice when pretraining already captures the retriever's behavior.

nodes.name: Scaling to 14B escapes plateaus
nodes.description: Increasing the rewriter to 14B breaks the performance plateaus of the 4B and 8B models, with larger models exploring more diversely (lower initial reward, better final policies).

nodes.name: 14B discovers statement-style queries
nodes.description: Under exploratory prompts the 14B model discovers statement-style rewrites: 'Being white and Latino' reaches nDCG@10 0.965 versus 0.542 for the question-style 'Can someone be both white and Latino?'.

nodes.name: Branching rollout
nodes.description: A two-turn branching rollout samples M first-turn actions and N second-turn completions each (e.g., 4x4), estimating first-turn value by Monte Carlo averaging and isolating the second-turn learning signal because the shared first-round reward cancels in the advantage.

nodes.name: Branching stabilizes training
nodes.description: The 4x4 branching strategy significantly outperforms independent 16x1 rollouts in training stability, preventing the collapse seen in the independent baseline.

nodes.name: More retrieval steps help
nodes.description: Increasing the number of retrieval steps improves query formulation because the model can use documents from earlier steps to refine later queries.

isolated_nodes.name: Weighted turn rewards
isolated_nodes.description: In multi-turn retrieval, trajectory reward is a weighted sum of per-turn nDCG, with weight 0.5 on the first retrieval and 1 on the second, and retrieved documents are masked from the loss.

isolated_nodes.name: Finance is a stress test
isolated_nodes.description: Finance serves as a stress test for transfer due to domain-specific terminology, hybrid text-and-table documents and practical relevance.

isolated_nodes.name: Retrieval gains improve RAG
isolated_nodes.description: Better retrieval translates into improved end-to-end RAG answer accuracy.

structural_reasoning: Retriever differences motivate RL rewriting; results, drift analysis, prompt-guidance, scaling and branching analyses follow.
